Advises reverse image search and no transfers to people not met in person.

sources.title: Regulatory and Executive Impersonation for WhatsApp Account Takeover using Malicious Windows Executables and High value financial fraud (TAU/ADV/017)
sources.publisher: I4C National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, MHA
sources.notes: Describes the 'Boss Scam': executives are sent malicious archives posing as urgent RBI/regulatory compliance, which hijack their WhatsApp Web session; fraudsters then message finance staff from the real account (or a number saved as 'CEO') instructing immediate payments to mule accounts. Advises finance teams to verify urgent payment requests by direct voice call or in person.

sources.title: IRCTC HeliYatra (Shri Kedarnath Dham helicopter booking portal)
sources.notes: Official portal states that helicopter services for the Shri Kedarnath Dham Yatra can be booked only through the IRCTC official website. Fetched via direct download because WebFetch got 403.

sources.title: MHA think tank alerts against hijack, sextortion scams on social media
sources.notes: Reports a BPRD (MHA police think tank) advisory on WhatsApp frauds: unknown video calls used for nude-recording sextortion; account hijacking where the takeover account asks the victim's contacts for money; and impersonation of a CEO/senior officer using a fake profile to demand urgent payments, citing a new number or an important meeting. Advises 2FA and not answering unknown calls.

sources.title: CBIC mounting multi-modal awareness against frauds in name of Customs
sources.publisher: Kashmir Reader (reporting Ministry of Finance / CBIC release)
sources.notes: Reports the Finance Ministry/CBIC awareness campaign: fraudsters posing as courier staff or Customs/Police/CBI officials claim a parcel or gift from abroad is held and demand duty or clearance fees, sometimes alleging contraband. CBIC states Customs officers never call, SMS or email asking for duty into private accounts, and genuine communications carry a verifiable DIN; report at cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.

sources.title: Delhi Police arrest man who duped women via dating apps and matrimonial sites
sources.publisher: Kerala Kaumudi (Delhi Police cyber cell case)
sources.notes: Delhi Police cyber cell arrested a man who posed as a doctor, businessman, film producer or lawyer on dating apps, matrimonial sites and Instagram, spent months building emotional connections with women, then asked for money citing medical emergencies, business losses or family problems; police said about Rs 2 crore was taken from over 500 women.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Police cybercrime advisory on AI voice cloning
sources.publisher: MediaNama (Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing advisory)
sources.notes: Tamil Nadu Cyber Crime Wing warned that scammers harvest voice samples from social media videos or 'wrong number' calls, clone the voice with AI, then call the person's contacts in a distressed tone asking for urgent money via UPI. Advises probing questions, verifying identity through a known channel and reporting to 1930.

sources.title: A new scam on the rise: Strangers stripping on video calls to extort money
sources.notes: Describes nude video-call recording via dating apps, Facebook and Sharechat, sometimes using morphed footage; follow-up calls from a fake Superintendent of Police claiming the woman attempted or died by suicide and a case would be filed, and fake YouTube staff offering to delete the video for a fee. Victims paid in repeated instalments; quotes Rachakonda police warnings.

sources.title: Public advisory on fraudsters using armed forces personnel details to perpetrate financial cyber frauds
sources.publisher: Nicobar Times (Andaman and Nicobar Police advisory)
sources.notes: Andaman and Nicobar Police warned that fraudsters misuse Indian Army personnel identities to target people advertising property for rent on housing platforms and social media. Advises verifying prospective renters separately, being wary of urgency, and remembering OTPs/PINs are needed to send money, not to receive it.

sources.title: Diglipur woman duped of Rs 5.22 lakh by cyber fraudsters
sources.notes: A Facebook friend posing as a UK benefactor moved the chat to WhatsApp and said gifts had reached Delhi Airport; a fake customs official demanded release fees, and the woman paid Rs 5.22 lakh via Google Pay to personal bank accounts before a further Rs 4.99 lakh demand alerted her.

sources.title: Mayabunder resident duped of INR 3,57,000 in KBC lottery scam offering INR 25,00,000 winnings
sources.notes: A resident got a WhatsApp call saying she had won Rs 25 lakh in a KBC lottery, shared bank details, photo and Aadhaar, and paid 'processing fees and taxes' in 14 transactions to multiple bank accounts totalling Rs 3.57 lakh.

sources.title: Rangat woman loses Rs 2.7 lakh in online fraud after fake police call about her son being involved in rape case
sources.notes: A caller posing as police said the woman's son was named in a rape case and would be arrested, with a voice resembling her son in the background, and demanded money to settle with officers and the victim's family; she paid Rs 2.7 lakh in multiple transfers. Police stressed that they do not take money to drop cases.

sources.title: Engineer corners Rs 118 flood aid with fake ID resembling Kerala CM's
sources.notes: A fraudster registered a look-alike UPI ID differing by one letter from the Kerala Chief Minister's Distress Relief Fund ID to catch flood-relief donations; Kerala Police had NPCI/SBI remove it and arrested him in Mumbai. Article notes the difference is hard to spot at a glance.

sources.title: Nigerian cheats Kottayam woman, loots money; arrested in Delhi
sources.notes: A fake Facebook friend 'from the UK' told a housewife a valuable gift was sent; a caller posing as a diplomatic agent at Mumbai Customs demanded Rs 22,000 duty, followed by more 'customs officers' at other airports who threatened legal action; she sold gold and took loans, losing Rs 81 lakh to named bank accounts.

sources.title: Union Home Minister reviews National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 and directs to make it better
sources.notes: Describes the official route for getting defrauded money back in India: CFCFRMS blocks fraudulent transactions through banks, an MHA SOP (January 2026) coordinates banks and police to return blocked funds, and a Money Restoration Module and Grievance Redressal Module have benefited about one lakh citizens. Fetched via direct download because WebFetch got 403.

sources.title: Cyber Crimes Through Fake Sites
sources.publisher: PIB, Ministry of Home Affairs (Rajya Sabha written reply)
sources.notes: MoS Home reply: NCRB does not separately record fake-website frauds; NCRP added a 'Report Suspect' feature (31 Jan 2024) for suspicious URLs (5,252 reported by then) and a facility to check a website's authenticity under 'Suspect Data'; I4C with NIXI disabled 310 malicious .in domains (Oct 2023-May 2024) and 91 phishing/fake websites. Fetched via direct download because WebFetch got 403.

sources.title: I4C cautions corporates and finance professionals against 'Boss Scam': WhatsApp account takeover through malicious 'Statement of Account', 'MCA' and 'RBI' files aimed at high-value financial fraud
sources.notes: I4C reports a sharp rise in NCRP complaints (Delhi, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan) of WhatsApp takeover via malicious 'Statement of Account'/RBI/MCA zip files; the hijacked senior executive's account, or a number saved as 'CEO', then instructs finance staff to make urgent transfers to mule accounts. Advises verifying any urgent fund-transfer instruction by direct voice call or in person; says I4C alerted over 58,000 potential victims in 30 days.

sources.title: When your voice is no longer proof
sources.notes: Opinion piece citing a Kolkata case where a 67-year-old sent Rs 95,990 within an hour to a caller who cloned an acquaintance's voice and claimed a relative was hospitalised. Notes there is no separate national figure for AI voice-clone fraud and repeats the government's 'Pause, Verify, Report' advice and 1930 helpline.

sources.title: Family member in distress or an AI voice clone? The rise of a disturbing new cyber crime scam
sources.notes: Describes a Noida mother who paid Rs 60,000 by UPI after a call in her son's cloned voice saying he was under threat; she later noticed he used an unfamiliar form of address. Experts advise calling back on a known number and agreeing family code words; cites a McAfee survey that 66% of Indian respondents would likely respond to urgent money calls from relatives.

sources.title: Cyber frauds exploiting goodwill of security forces to dupe people online
sources.notes: Fraudsters pose as army or paramilitary personnel on OLX and Quikr, offering cheap vehicles or goods because they are 'transferred', sending fake service ID cards and asking for small advances; others send QR codes or payment links that debit sellers. Notes a CISF public warning on 4 Sep 2020 and advises not dealing with anyone who only shows an unverified official ID.

sources.title: VHP raises alarm about fake messages on social media soliciting donations in guise of donations for Ram Mandir
sources.notes: Cybercriminals circulated social media messages and calls seeking donations for the Ram Temple with QR codes that sent money to fraudsters; when a VHP worker posed as a donor, the caller asked for a WhatsApp number to send a QR code. VHP complained to MHA and Delhi/UP police and said the temple trust had authorised no fundraising.

sources.title: Fraudsters posing as Army personnel and invoking nationalism execute unique crime in Hyderabad
sources.notes: A fake Army officer tenant using 'Jai Hind' messaging had an 'Army accountant' ask a Secunderabad owner to send Rs 5 as a 'reversal mode' test (returned to build trust), then the advance and repeated amounts so the 'system' would credit them back; she lost Rs 1.3 lakh. Police warned not to blindly believe people claiming to be from the Army.

sources.title: Hyderabad man loses over Rs 12.75 lakh in house rental cyber fraud
sources.publisher: The Week (PTI, citing Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police)
sources.notes: A flat owner who listed on a real-estate portal was called by a fake NSG commando 'being transferred' and his 'senior officer', who cited a special defence security protocol requiring him to pay first to 'raise a demand' for an Rs 80,000 advance; he lost Rs 12.75 lakh in IMPS/UPI transfers. Police warned of Army/NSG impersonation targeting property owners with forged IDs.

sources.title: OLX scams on the rise again in Tamil Nadu, customers fall prey to fake 'army men'
sources.notes: Buyer-side variant: a fake army officer lists a scooter or car, claims a transfer, sends an ID card, insists on advance payment by Google Pay because outsiders cannot enter the camp, then demands more money. Tamil Nadu cyber crime cell reported about 100 such complaints since January 2020.

sources.title: Fraudsters targeting families of students
sources.notes: Fake police called parents of Chandigarh school students claiming the child was held in a drug case, put a crying girl on the line, told the parent not to hang up and demanded Rs 50,000 for release. Police advised verifying callers, never paying unfamiliar numbers and reporting to 1930.

sources.title: Kapurthala farmer loses Rs 11.75 lakh in cyber fraud
sources.notes: Callers told a Punjab couple their son in Canada had caused a serious accident, then posed as officials warning of legal consequences, claimed the son's phone was with police and told them not to contact him; they transferred Rs 11.75 lakh from two bank accounts without telling anyone.

sources.title: 2 Nigerians dupe women on pretext of marriage, arrested
sources.notes: Men posing as UK-based marine engineers contacted women on marriage websites, shared a flight ticket, then a woman posing as a Mumbai airport official said the 'groom' was detained with foreign currency and needed customs clearance fees; one victim paid about Rs 4 lakh in several payments.

sources.title: App date turns costly for civil services aspirant
sources.notes: A Tinder match invited a man to a Delhi cafe for her 'birthday', left early, and the cafe presented a bill of about Rs 1.22 lakh; he was threatened and forced to pay online. Police said the bill was split between the woman, managers and owners and described a wider scheme in metro cities, noting stigma stops victims reporting.

sources.title: Man blackmails people posing as YouTube employee, nabbed
sources.notes: Delhi Police arrested a man who befriended victims on social media, recorded them in compromising WhatsApp video calls, then posed as a YouTube employee and as a Delhi Police cyber crime inspector, demanding money not to upload the footage. One complainant paid over Rs 25 lakh across multiple transactions.

sources.title: Kerala Police warns public against fake WhatsApp gift scam using popular brand names
sources.notes: Kerala Police warned of WhatsApp messages using dairy and other well-known brand names and logos to offer 'anniversary gifts' and 'free gifts', with links to fake look-alike company portals that aim to steal money and personal information. Full article partly paywalled.

sources.title: Mann Ki Baat, episode 115: 'Stop, Think, Take Action'
sources.notes: 'There is no system like digital arrest in the law'; no agency questions people on phone or video calls; 'Ruko, Socho, Action Lo'

sources.title: Alert against 'digital arrest' by cyber criminals impersonating state and central agencies
sources.notes: How digital arrest, parcel and 'relative in custody' frauds work; organised cross-border syndicates

sources.title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 344: financial cyber fraud
sources.notes: ₹22,845.73 crore reported and 19,18,865 financial-fraud complaints on NCRP in 2024

sources.title: Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question 1505: digital arrest scams
sources.notes: 1,23,672 digital-arrest incidents and ₹1,935.51 crore defrauded in 2024 (NCRP)

sources.title: Action against task-based and investment fraud websites
sources.notes: How part-time 'like and review' task frauds escalate into deposits

sources.title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and helpline 1930
sources.notes: 'Any victim of financial cyber fraud can dial helpline number 1930'

sources.title: Financial fraud awareness brochures
sources.notes: Impersonation of relatives and hospital staff in 'emergency' calls

sources.title: UPI safety
sources.notes: 'UPI PIN is NOT required for receiving money'

sources.title: BE(A)WARE: modus operandi of financial fraudsters
sources.publisher: Reserve Bank of India, Office of the RBI Ombudsman
sources.notes: Vishing, screen sharing, QR codes, fake customer care, lottery and job frauds; 'no need to enter PIN / password anywhere to receive money'; a genuine company 'will never ask for money' for a job

sources.title: Discussion Paper: Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds
sources.notes: 2025: 28 lakh frauds, ₹22,931 crore; 98.5% of fraud value in payments above ₹10,000; proposed 1-hour lag and a 'trusted person'

sources.title: RBI Kehta Hai: be cautious
sources.notes: 'RBI or your bank will never ask for these' (OTP, PIN, CVV); unsolicited lottery messages are fake

sources.title: RBI Kehta Hai: digital arrest
sources.notes: 'There is nothing like digital arrest' (Hindi page: 'डिजिटल अरेस्ट जैसी कोई चीज़ नहीं होती')

sources.title: RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation
sources.notes: Unsolicited calls and links threatening to freeze or block accounts; contact the bank directly

sources.title: Customer liability in fraudulent electronic banking transactions (RBI/2026-27/167)
sources.notes: Covers payments made 'under coercion or duress'; customer negligence includes ignoring 'specific, directed and clear warnings from the bank'

sources.title: RBI cautions public against fictitious offers of money from abroad
sources.notes: 'Nobody from RBI calls up people about lottery winnings/funds received from abroad'

sources.title: RBI cautions against sharing PIN, UPI PIN and OTP
sources.notes: Never share PIN, UPI PIN or OTP 'not even with bank officials'

sources.title: SEBI advisory against fraudulent trading schemes (PR 4/2024) and 'Fake trading app scam' explainer
sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.notes: 'There is no provision for an Institutional Account in trading'; guaranteed returns in the securities market are a scam

sources.title: TRAI cautions public against impersonation
sources.notes: 'No regulatory body conducts investigations or collects payments through phone calls, messaging apps, or video platforms'
